freshness_note: Every citation on a mover, volume outlier, or recommendation card carries the actual publish date of its source, separate from this page's pull date above. Price/volume/index data always refreshes live on pull; narrative research is only rewritten when genuinely newer reporting was found for that name - otherwise the existing writeup stands rather than being re-presented under a fresher-looking timestamp. Data note (this pull, 2026-09-22): the free Yahoo Finance bulk endpoint this dashboard uses for the full ~1,500-name universe had not yet posted Monday, Sept 21 daily bars for individual equities at pull time, even though the major index tickers (S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow, Russell 2000, VIX - tracked separately on Point 1 and above) had already updated through Monday's close. The gainers/losers/volume tables below therefore reflect Friday, Sept 18's session (the most recent complete session with individual-equity data actually available), one trading day behind the index-level data elsewhere on this dashboard - every citation is dated accordingly rather than presented as Monday news.

top_gainers.name: MARA Holdings, Inc.
top_gainers.narrative: MARA Holdings led bitcoin-miner stocks higher (+13.7%) as bitcoin broke above $80,000-81,000 resistance on Sept 18, with Morgan Stanley nearly doubling its price target to $11 from $6 (still Underweight-rated, but a notable reassessment of downside risk) and H.C. Wainwright initiating coverage at Buy with a $20 target, explicitly citing MARA's strategic pivot from pure bitcoin mining toward AI-focused data-center infrastructure as the thesis. Consensus among 12 covering analysts is mixed (8 Buy, 1 Hold, 3 Sell, average target $18.70), reflecting real disagreement over whether the AI pivot re-rates the stock or just adds execution risk on top of bitcoin-price beta.

top_gainers.name: Coinbase
top_gainers.narrative: Coinbase jumped 11.7% on Friday, Sept 18 to $194.25, becoming the S&P 500's top percentage gainer that session, as bitcoin broke through $80,000-81,000 resistance it had struggled against for weeks. The move wasn't purely a bitcoin-beta trade: the SEC's new five-year conditional 'Innovation Exemption' (letting eligible platforms trade tokenized U.S. stocks on blockchain venues without full exchange registration) and Coinbase's own filing to list the first U.S. single-stock perpetual futures both landed the same day, giving the stock company-specific catalysts on top of the crypto market-wide rally.

citations.title: Strategy Climbs 12%, Coinbase Jumps 10% as Bitcoin Tops $80,000
Coinbase Stock Jumped 12% Last Friday. Bitcoin's Breakout Wasn't the Only Reason.

top_gainers.name: Sandisk
top_gainers.narrative: Sandisk surged 11% on Friday, Sept 18 to $1,791.82 (an intraday high of $1,797, just shy of $1,800), extending a run that's up 580% in 2026, on reports of further NAND flash/SSD price increases amid a tightening global memory (DRAM/NAND) supply picture - AI data-center demand for memory keeps growing while supply lags. Intel's reported plan to raise processor prices roughly 10% in October added a second tailwind, boosting sentiment across storage and semiconductor names generally; unusually heavy call-option activity was also a factor in the size of the move.

citations.title: SanDisk Stock Price Prediction: Surges 11% on Heavy Volume to Approach $1,800

top_gainers.name: Robinhood Markets
top_gainers.narrative: Robinhood rose 9.1% on Friday, Sept 18 (surging as much as 9.6% intraday to near $120) after the SEC announced a five-year conditional 'Innovation Exemption' letting eligible platforms trade tokenized versions of U.S. stocks on blockchain venues without full traditional exchange registration - a direct regulatory tailwind for Robinhood, which already operates its own Layer-2 blockchain (Robinhood Chain) and offers tokenized equities overseas, positioning it to capture domestic tokenized-securities share ahead of less-prepared competitors. Bitcoin's break above $80,000-81,000 the same day added a second, market-wide tailwind.

top_losers.name: Peabody Energy, Inc.
top_losers.narrative: Peabody Energy fell 7.4% (touching $25.60 intraday) on Friday, Sept 18, extending a decline that has taken the stock down 29% over the trailing 90 days. The proximate driver is company-specific, not macro: a securities-fraud class action was filed on behalf of Peabody investors alleging the company misled the market about coal production problems at Centurion, its flagship premium hard-coking-coal mine, after the stock had already dropped more than 9% on the underlying production news. Not a read-through to the coal/energy sector broadly - this is a single-name legal/operational overhang.

citations.title: Peabody Energy (NYSE:BTU) Stock Price Down 5.8% - What's Next?
Peabody Energy Stock Falls as Fraud Suit Cites Mine Woes

top_losers.name: Qualcomm
top_losers.narrative: Qualcomm fell 5.8% on Friday, Sept 18, closing at $177.72 - the S&P 500's session standout decliner even as the broader chip sector rallied on the Meta-Muse-driven CPU-demand story the same week. Multiple headwinds converged: positioning-driven profit-taking after a strong prior rally, a stretched valuation, specific competitive concerns (weaker Apple-modem share, Samsung Exynos gains), and a hawkish repricing of Fed rate expectations weighing on high-multiple tech names generally. No single catalyst dominates - this reads as a multi-factor reversal of Qualcomm's own recent run rather than a sector- or market-wide move (the broader market/chip sector was up the same week).

citations.title: Qualcomm Drops 6% as Past Month's Rally Unwinds; Skyworks and Qorvo Slip

bounce.name: Enova International, Inc.
bounce.thesis: Enova crashed ~22-25% on Sept 15 after withdrawing its OCC/Fed regulatory applications for the $369M Grasshopper Bancorp acquisition, with the CEO citing a lack of clear standards for nonbanks seeking to become banks. This is a real, abandoned strategic deal, not noise - but the company reiterated Q3 and full-year 2026 guidance unchanged (revenue +25% y/y, adjusted EPS +30% y/y) the same day, meaning the core lending business's outlook wasn't cut. Bounce thesis rests on the deal's collapse being a strategic setback rather than a signal of operational trouble.

citations.title: Enova International (ENVA) Stock Plummets 25% After Abandoning $369M Grasshopper Bank Acquisition

bounce.name: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals
bounce.thesis: Arrowhead fell on continued concerns about cash burn ($194.3M net loss last quarter) despite genuine clinical progress: SHASTA trial results showed a 78% reduction in acute pancreatitis events, and REDEMPLO revenue roughly doubled quarter over quarter. Piper Sandler maintained an Overweight rating through the decline. This looks like a financing/burn-rate overhang on an otherwise-advancing pipeline rather than a thesis-breaking clinical setback - the bounce case depends on that read being right.

citations.title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals (ARWR) Stock Retreats As Losses Deepen Behind Phase III Progress

value.name: CoStar Group
value.thesis: CoStar is down ~68% from its 52-week high despite revenue still growing 21% with a 79% gross margin - the market has re-rated the stock hard on competitive/execution concerns (its residential push against Zillow) rather than a revenue collapse. Classic value setup if the core commercial real estate data business keeps compounding while the market has priced in near-failure of the residential bet.

value.name: Fiserv
value.thesis: Fiserv is down 64% over the past year after slashing 2026 guidance to roughly flat organic revenue, driven partly by Argentina inflation normalization. Real fundamental deterioration, not pure sentiment - but at 72% below one fair-value estimate ($48.65 vs $174.38 GuruFocus GF Value), this is a case where the market may have overcorrected for a genuine but bounded problem.

citations.title: Fiserv stock tumbles after cutting 2026 guidance

value.name: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions
value.thesis: Kratos is down 37% YTD despite a strong defense backlog and hypersonics revenue guided to ~$400M in 2026 and $700M+ in 2027 (MACH-TB program funding), plus recent $20M and $35M contract wins. Value case: the stock's multiple has compressed even as the forward revenue/earnings trajectory improved.

value.name: Duolingo
value.thesis: Duolingo is down 41% YTD after management deliberately chose user growth over near-term monetization (guiding 2026 bookings growth to ~11% vs the ~20% it could have delivered under the old approach). This is a valuation reset (14.6x forward P/E vs a 3-year average of 88x), not a demand problem - the growth-first bet either pays off in re-accelerated bookings later, or it doesn't.

citations.title: Duolingo Stock Is Down 41% in 2026. Here's Why Investors Are Repricing Growth
